newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up on spreading, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up on spreading, Taiwan.

text.p: CME hog futures continued to show the bullish impact of the Taiwan pork ban as prices closed mostly higher, traders said.
Spreading and rolling of longs added to gains in deferred months while pressuring the nearby, they said.
Hog futures closed 0.375 cent lower to 0.675 higher with only April off at 72.800 cents. August paced the gain. Pork bellies finished 0.300 lower to 0.250 higher with May unchanged at 75.950 cents.
Rolling of long April positions into back months ahead of the Hogs and Pigs report and its assumption of the spot position next week weighed on the nearby, traders said.

The Taiwan pork ban continued to provide support, especially to summer months. Expectations are that demand for U.S. pork will be at its highest during the third quater as countries that had been importing from Taiwan use storage supplies for the time being. Japan especially has adequate pork stocks to meet immediate needs, they said.

Foot and mouth disease continues to spread in Taiwan with 716 breeding centers reporting infected hogs and estimates that about 15 percent of their 11 million head hog population would be affected directly.

In the meantime, the recent jump in domestic pork prices may have exasperated an already slow demand for pork due to high prices. Packers in turn are bidding lower for cash hogs, especially with marketings up, they said.
"There's no domestic demand right now and there's plenty of hogs," one trader said.

Evening up ahead of Thursday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report also started to influence the market and most of Thursday trade is expected to be position-squaring ahead of the report later in the day, they added.
Analyst estimates for all hogs averaged 99.2 percent in a range of 97 to 100.9 percent.
Hogs kept for breeding estimates averaged 101.4 percent and ranged 98.5 to 104 and hogs kept for market averaged 99 percent and ranged 96 to 100.8 percent.

Pork belly futures retreated from early gains on profit taking to end mostly lower. However, Tuesday's mildly bullish CME weekly out-of-town pork belly storage report and mostly higher hog futures provided underlying support, traders said.
The CME reported a net in-movement of 926,000 lbs in its weekly CME out-of-town storage report, less than early estimates of in 1.0 to 2.0 million lbs.

E.D.&F. Man, R.J. O'Brien and Rosenthal Collins bought April hogs before bear spreaders buying June and selling April dominated trade. Stone Traders and Rand Financials did the spread early and Prudential Securities late. E.D.&F. Man sold May bellies after buying by locals, LFG and Smith Barney, pit sources said.

In hog options, commission houses were doing early risk reversals ahead of the Hog and Pig report. Later they offered the July 70 straddle. ABN Chicogo Corp bought June 80 puts and sold 76 puts. Volatility was firm, pit sources added.
